business_type_notes: The whole niche is type D (a move: a dated event with the customer's belongings in someone else's hands) per the calibration pack, section 2: every GBP category (Removals Company, Removals Service, Self Storage Facility) and every page target, including office moves, storage, single items, pianos, antiques and house clearance. No category differs. The split inside D is by the stage of the move, written into the briefs, not the type: a home move reads the stages of moving day (survey and pack, load, the wait between homes, unload and place); an office move the stages of a business move (out of hours timing, labelling, IT and furniture, open by opening time); packing and dismantling the preparation stage; storage the stage between homes; single items and pianos one short day for one piece; house clearance the stages of a clearance (authority, what is kept, what goes where, the house left empty). No page is desire led, problem led or symptom led: type D has no symptoms and no faults. A client hand set to type A has no briefs in this entry (the hand set-up defaults to A: set D).

faq_slots.question: Will my furniture fit into the new place?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned local situation (an access situation, not a fault: terrace stairs with a turn at the top, a flat above a shop, a third floor with no lift, a parking court the lorry cannot enter) and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different things that decide it, from the trade facts Table B signs rows: the route itself (doors, stairs, landings and the turns between them), the piece (beds and wardrobes come apart; a sofa loses its feet and doors; a piano goes on its own equipment), and where the van can stand (a long carry, or a smaller van to shuttle). Then what the survey settles about it before the day. Dismantling in the quote only as the services list has it. Never promise it will fit, never force it (Table B done badly).

faq_slots.question: Should I pack myself or have you pack?

A packing service only where the services list has one; link the page where LINKABLE PAGES has it. Never a number of boxes or a packing time.

faq_slots.question: Do I need to arrange parking for the van?

Say it is worth looking at the parking at both addresses before the day. No lead time, no fee, no council named. Never that parking in the area is impossible.

faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts rule rows only, put as what usually applies, in plain words. What is the customer's: a parking suspension where the street needs one (apply to the council); on a clearance, checking the clearer is a registered waste carrier on the public register; on an international move, the customs paperwork the move needs, only as the client confirms it handles it; on a storage contract, what the agreement says about release and redelivery.
